text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Negotiations between Tele Danmark and French tv company Canal + have failed to produce a concrete alliance but collaboration remains possible. Canal + wants to relaunch its so far unsuccesful FilmNet 1 and 2 and SuperSport on a new Nordic Canal+ channel and a Danish Canal+ Gold.

--Retailers are changing their attitude to large shopping centres in the face of evidence from Jutland that the opening of several big centres has not forced small shops out of business. The small retailers are beginning to see the competition as healthy, rather than unfair.
--EU approval of weedkillers banned in Denmark could have serious consequences for continued Danish membership, environment minister Svend Auken says.
--Nykredit directors last night rejected their chief executive's plan to deepen a sales and marketing alliance with third biggest bank BG Bank and leading insurer Topdanmark.

--Swedish telecoms company Telia is striving hard to be number two in Denmark, after Tele Danmark, despite losing 100 million crowns locally in 1996. In traffic and new connections it is already number two.
--Copenhagen is to reduce commercial property tax by one seventh over three years, says Lord Mayor Jens Kramer Mikkelsen, who has put helping business at the top of his agenda.
--Tax Minister Carsten Koch has set up a special unit to monitor the accounts of multinational companies.
